Argentine Oil & Gas Producers Association Names New Executive Director

BUENOS AIRES, June 12 – The Oil & Gas Producers Association of Argentina (OGPA) on Wednesday announced the appointment of Verónica Salazar as its new executive director, a move industry participants say signals renewed focus on sustainable growth and regulatory engagement in the country’s vital energy sector.

Salazar, 48, brings more than two decades of experience in energy policy and corporate leadership, most recently serving as director of government affairs at Energía Austral, a leading upstream operator. She succeeds Martín Fernández, who held the post since 2016 and is retiring after a 35-year career in the industry. Salazar will assume her new duties on July 1.

“I am honored by the trust the board has placed in me at a pivotal time for Argentina’s oil and gas sector,” Salazar said in a statement released by the OGPA. “My top priorities will be fostering collaboration among producers, strengthening our dialogue with regulators, and advancing initiatives that drive responsible growth and investment.”

Argentina’s oil and gas industry has experienced steady expansion in recent years, buoyed by the development of the Vaca Muerta shale formation in Neuquén province. According to government data, the country produced 256 million barrels of crude oil and 48 billion cubic meters of natural gas in 2023, representing annual increases of 7% and 4% respectively.

OGPA chair Alejandro Luján praised Salazar’s “deep understanding of both the technical and policy challenges facing the sector,” noting her experience in stakeholder engagement and environmental stewardship. “We are confident Verónica will strengthen the association’s role as a constructive partner for government and society,” Luján said.

Industry analysts welcomed the appointment, citing Salazar’s track record in advocating for regulatory clarity and investment incentives. “Her leadership comes at a time when Argentina needs to balance production growth with climate goals and community expectations,” said Silvia Rosetti, senior analyst at the Buenos Aires-based consultancy Energía Futuro.

The OGPA represents more than 30 domestic and international companies operating in Argentina, collectively accounting for over 90% of the nation’s hydrocarbon output. The association works closely with provincial and federal authorities on policy, safety standards, and workforce development.

Salazar holds degrees in petroleum engineering from the National University of La Plata and a master’s in public administration from the University of Buenos Aires.
